version.changelog: Initial release - Glances cross-system monitoring tool skill

llm.summary: This Glances monitoring skill is coherent, but it includes under-scoped examples that can expose host telemetry, install software, and create persistent services or scheduled tasks.

dimensions.detail: The documented Web UI, API, remote monitoring, Docker monitoring, exports, alerts, and troubleshooting commands fit a Glances system-monitoring skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Several guides tell the AI it can directly run install, server-start, remote binding, export, and troubleshooting commands without consistently requiring explicit user confirmation or localhost-first defaults.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package is markdown-only with no bundled executable installer, but it instructs use of pip, system package managers, Docker pulls, and optional dependency installs that modify the user's environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Examples bind Web/API/server modes to 0.0.0.0 and document process lists, full snapshots, Docker status, and metric exports with limited warnings about authentication, firewalling, or sensitive telemetry exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The advanced guide includes Docker socket mounts, host PID/network modes, systemd service creation, cron alerting, sudo usage, and plaintext credential examples; these are purpose-aligned but high-impact and not sufficiently scoped.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review commands before allowing an agent to run them. Prefer pipx or local-only installs, bind Web/API/server modes to 127.0.0.1 unless remote access is intentional, require authentication and firewall or VPN controls for remote endpoints, avoid Docker socket or host namespace options unless needed, and do not place real tokens or passwords in shared or world-readable config files.
llm.findings:
[SDI-2] expected: Starting a Web UI is expected for Glances, but the quickstart's all-interface binding example can expose monitoring data beyond the local machine without a clear warning.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote Web/API/server features and metric endpoints are normal monitoring capabilities, but the docs under-disclose the sensitivity of process, host, Docker, and full snapshot data when reachable over a network.
[SQP-2] expected: Package installation and optional dependency setup are expected, but the skill uses execution-oriented wording for environment-changing commands without clear approval and least-privilege guidance.
[SQP-2] expected: Docker host monitoring is relevant, but mounting container engine sockets and using host PID/network options grants broad host visibility and should require explicit opt-in.
[SQP-2] expected: Export and alert configuration is relevant, but examples place placeholder passwords and tokens in config files and create cron-based notifications without enough secret-handling or persistence warnings.
